 239,131 RAM 1500s Recalled Because the Backup Camera Can Go Blank in Reverse
 MotorBiscuit Rahaan Mazumder Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC If you own a late-model Ram pickup truck, it is officially time to run your Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) through the federal database. Over the course of just five weeks, Chrysler (FCA US) has issued three separate safety recalls covering up to 263,845 Ram 1500 and 2500 pickups.
 Because a single 2026 Ram 1500 could potentially be entangled in multiple active campaigns, it is crucial to check which fixes apply specifically to your vehicle. Currently, there are zero reports of crashes or injuries associated with any of these three defects.
 RAMs Quarter-Million Camera Blackout
 The vast majority of the affected vehicles fall under a massive software recall that initiated owner notifications on September 24.
 Advertisement Advertisement Under NHTSA Campaign Number 26V560 (Chrysler recall number 83D ), the automaker recalled 239,131 Ram 1500 trucks from the 2025 and 2026 model years. The issue impacts trucks built between October 6, 2023, and February 23, 2026.
 2026 Ram 1500 | Ram
 Due to a flawed radio software package, the infotainment screen may simply go blank instead of displaying the rearview camera image when the driver shifts into reverse. The remedy is a free software update. Owners have the option to receive the fix remotely via an Over-the-Air (OTA) update, or they can schedule an appointment to have a dealer flash the radio in person.
 Failing Sensors and Stability Control
 While the camera blackout covers the highest volume of trucks, Ram has rapidly followed it up with two fresh hardware recalls for the 2026 model year.
 Under NHTSA Campaign Number 26V623 , Ram recalled 16,385 of its 2026 Ram 1500 pickups for a critical sensor failure. The internal TPMS sensors may fail to detect low tire pressure and subsequently fail to illuminate the dashboard warning light, placing the trucks out of compliance with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) 138. Owner notification letters began rolling out around October 27, and dealers will inspect and replace the faulty sensors free of charge.
 Advertisement Advertisement Simultaneously, heavy-duty owners have their own defect to address. Under NHTSA Campaign Number 26V651 , Ram recalled 8,329 of its 2026 Ram 2500 trucks. A defective steering column control module can cause a sudden loss of Electronic Stability Control (ESC), violating FMVSS 126. This action actually expands upon an earlier recall (26V244) for the same module. Owner letters for this ESC fix are scheduled to be mailed by November 24, and dealers will replace the module for free.
 Owners who want to check their status before physical letters arrive in the mail can enter their 17-character VIN at NHTSA.gov/recalls or call Chrysler customer service directly at 1-800-853-1403 .
